find: A Jacobean audience, for whom mercy was a Christian duty, would have found Shylock’s refusal shocking
replace: An Elizabethan audience, for whom mercy was a Christian duty, would have found Shylock’s refusal shocking
note: F2: the play was written c.1596–97, under Elizabeth I. A model AO3 sentence must not call that audience Jacobean.

expect: The three AQA assessment objectives for Shakespeare are AO1 (quotation), AO2 (language and _____), and AO3 (context).
value: AQA marks the Shakespeare question on AO1 (quotation), AO2 (language and _____), AO3 (context) and AO4 (spelling and grammar).
note: F3: AQA assesses four AOs on Paper 1 Section A (AO4 carries the 4 SPaG marks). The lesson's own content and exam tip say four.

find: “Let no sound of shallow foppery enter / My sober house”
replace: “Let not the sound of shallow foppery enter / My sober house”
note: F4: the line reads “Let not the sound of shallow fopp’ry enter / My sober house” (2.5).

expect: How does Shakespeare present Shylock’s reaction to Jessica’s elopement? Refer to Act 3, Scene 1 in your answer.

expect: A monkey — a callous trade for Shylock's wedding gift.
value: A monkey — a callous trade for the ring Leah gave Shylock before they married.
note: F7: Shylock says “I had it of Leah when I was a bachelor” (3.1), so it was not a wedding gift.
